narration.full_text: Alright students, time for some more quick questions to test your understanding of Control and Coordination! Let's dive in. First question: The growth of pollen tubes towards ovules is an example of which tropism? Is it Hydrotropism, Geotropism, Chemotropism, or Phototropism? Think carefully about the chemical signals involved. The correct answer is (c) Chemotropism. Pollen tubes grow in response to chemical stimuli from the ovule. Next question: How do the shoot and roots of a plant respond to the pull of Earth's gravity? Consider their typical growth directions. Roots grow downwards, towards gravity, exhibiting positive geotropism. Shoots usually grow upwards and away from the Earth, showing negative geotropism. Moving on, can you explain the cause of shoots of the plant bending towards light? What hormone is involved here? Stems are positively phototropic and bend towards light due to more auxin accumulating on the darker side. This causes greater growth on the darker side, bending the stem towards the light source. And finally, define positive geotropism and negative geotropism. Give one example of each. Geotropism is the movement of a plant part in response to gravity. Roots show positive geotropism by growing towards gravity. Stems show negative geotropism by growing away from gravity. Great job, everyone! Keep up the excellent work!

visual_beats.description: Title: More Questions: Control and Coordination

Question: The growth of pollen tubes towards ovules is the example of:
(a) Hydrotropism
(b) Geotropism
(c) Chemotropism
(d) Phototropism
Question: How do the shoot and roots of a plant respond to the pull of earth's gravity?
Answer: Roots grow downwards, towards gravity while shoot usually grow upwards and away from earth.
Question: Explain the cause of shoots of the plant bending towards light.

Answer: Stems are positively phototropic and bend towards the direction of light. The movement is due to occurrence of more auxin on the darker side and lesser auxin on the illuminated side. Thus there is more growth on the darker side which causes the stem to bend towards light.
Question: Define positive geotropism and negative geotropism. Give one example of each.

Answer: The movement of plant part in response to gravity is called geotropic movement and the phenomenon involved is called geotropism. When the tip of the stem grows away from the earth's gravitational forces, it is known as negative geotropism and when the root tips grow towards gravity, it is known as positive geotropism. E.g., Stem shows negative geotropism. Roots show positive geotropism.
